result: 1 passed in 34.71s against a local self-hosted Prefect API and PostgreSQL 16 container.
assertions: A durable CSV-to-PostgreSQL submission is dispatched to a separate Process worker. The worker pauses at the connector commit boundary and confirms that no sink rows or effect records are visible before commit.

The separately supervised Prefect API is stopped while the worker is paused at connector commit. The connector commits once; while the API remains unavailable, PostgreSQL shows one sink row and one effect record, the canonical attempt remains running, the ETL report is succeeded, and result publication remains pending.
An authorized status read while the API is down preserves the canonical running state and reports remote orchestration and reconciliation as unavailable.

The API restarts against the same PostgreSQL database. The worker resumes host finalization and publishes the existing result; PostgreSQL still shows one sink row and effect record, and the canonical submission and attempt complete exactly once.

runtime.platform: macOS 26.5.2 arm64 host; PostgreSQL ran in Docker
runtime.prefect_server: Separately supervised self-hosted API process; stopped during connector commit and restarted before worker finalization

fingerprints.source_sha256_method: SHA-256 over sorted repository-relative source paths and file bytes, with NUL separators.

limitations: This is one local source-checkout integration run, not installed-wheel or multi-version CI evidence. The exact CPython patch matrix is recorded separately after the blocking installed-wheel workflow completes.

The outage lasts only across connector commit and host finalization. Prolonged API outages, simultaneous multi-process failures, sustained capacity, production hosting, third-party connectors, and a real 30-day retention interval remain unqualified.

ci_configuration.database_service: Temporary postgres:16 Docker container mapped to an ephemeral localhost port
ci_configuration.server_process: Separate Prefect API process with PostgreSQL persistence

cleanup: The test used unique tenant, workspace, submission, deployment, sink-table, effect-ledger, and Prefect database identities; test-owned tables and the dedicated Prefect database were removed.
The temporary PostgreSQL container was removed after the campaign.
